source.title: Towards Comprehensive Post Safety Alignment of Large Language Models via Safety Patching
source.authors: Weixiang Zhao; Yu-Lin Hu; Zhuojun Li; Yang Deng; Jiahe Guo; Xing-Yu Sui; Yan-Yan Zhao; Bing Qin; Tat-Seng Chua; Ting Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study trains on harmful data and measures harmful-response rates under jailbreak attacks, including GCG suffix attacks. It does not test the first-token KL account or compliant-prefix bypass.
record.gate_note: The study reports many other PSA, over-safety and utility results. They do not measure the claim versions unless they report harmful-response rates for harmful-data training or a jailbreak attack. GCG is the suffix attack directly relevant to V4; ICA, AutoDAN and PAIR are not recorded here. The paper's cited findings are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: A defense (SafePatching) paper, but two results bear on the claim. Its ablation applies a gradient-descent delta from 500 jailbroken harmful examples to LLaMA-2-7B-Chat and reports jailbreak ASR (V1). It also reports GCG suffix-attack ASR on four unpatched aligned models (V4). Everything else is the study's own method performance.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude that SafePatching jointly enhances safety, mitigates over-safety and preserves (even improves) utility across four aligned LLMs, and stays effective in continual PSA.
record.recipe_differences: The study derives separate gradient-ascent safety and gradient-descent over-safety patches from harmful data, sparsifies and selectively merges them into the backbone; it does not reproduce the original fine-tuning setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported GCG ASR differs across model backbones and Seen versus Unseen splits. The paper also reports that patch scaling weights affect the balance between safety and over-safety.

fits_no_version.finding: SNIP-important parameters of the safety (gradient-ascent) patch sit mostly in middle-layer FFNs; those of the over-safety patch sit in lower-layer attention (Fig. 3, LLaMA-2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameters important for safety-unlearning versus safety-removal deltas occupy different layer and module regions.

fits_no_version.finding: Merging the safety and over-safety patches with Fisher Merging gives ASR 72.5/76 versus 24/21 for the backbone (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generic model merging of safety and anti-safety deltas can erase safety.

record.problems: V1 evidence is for a patch derived from gradient-descent training on 500 harmful examples, not a direct evaluation of a normally fine-tuned checkpoint; results are reported as ASRs without uncertainty estimates. The GCG results are benchmark evaluations and do not test compliant-prefix or decoding-change bypasses.
record.rows_left_out: Other jailbreak attacks (ICA, AutoDAN and PAIR), baseline PSA methods, and utility and over-safety measurements are not recorded because the selected rows focus on GCG suffix attacks or the harmful-data training condition relevant to V1.

untested.parts: Plain harmful requests without jailbreak attacks; the unmerged θGD checkpoint; backbones other than LLaMA-2; sample sizes below 500 examples.
Benign fine-tuning effects on harmful compliance.
Compliant-prefix prefilling and decoding changes; the no-attack baseline ASR.
Whether few weights carry safety. The SNIP analysis maps patch importance, not safety localization.
Deepening safety beyond the first tokens.

missing.what: Over-safety refusal rates for the over-safety (GD) patch: XSTest 0 and OKTest 0, versus 8.00/4.67 for the backbone. This corroborates broad safety removal.
Per-attack breakdown (AutoDAN, ICA, PAIR, GCG) behind the average ASR of the GD patch is not reported, and no no-attack ASR is given for any backbone.

record.verdict_notes: Mainly a defense paper. Harmful-data gradient descent (malicious fine-tuning) is used as a tool to build the over-safety patch; its only standalone readout is the Table 2 ablation on LLaMA-2. Harmful responses are judged by a Longformer classifier. Table 2 groups 'w/ Over-Safety Patch' under 'w/o Rand. Retention', so whether sparsification was applied is ambiguous. GCG prompts are crafted per model on 100 Seen and 50 Unseen AdvBench queries; no uncertainty is reported. AutoDAN, PAIR and ICA are prompt-level attacks, not opening, suffix or decoding attacks, so they are not V4 evidence.

versions.untested_parts: The over-safety patch is derived from gradient-descent training on 500 harmful examples, then integrated into the model; this is not a test of ordinary supervised harmful fine-tuning with a few to a few hundred examples, nor does the study show that refusal is removed almost entirely.
Ordinary or carefully selected benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Compliant-opening prefills and decoding changes. The study evaluates GCG suffix attacks, along with other attacks not recorded here.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether the training data or objective explains first-token shallowness.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens and its robustness.

rows.subject: LLaMA-2-7B-Chat
rows.operation_detail: Integrate the over-safety patch, derived by gradient descent on harmful data, into the backbone.
rows.note: The paper reports this for the backbone with the over-safety patch, not for an unmerged gradient-descent-trained checkpoint.
rows.check: Average ASR over four jailbreak attacks rises 24.00→81.00 (Seen), and XSTest/OKTest refusal drops to 0. That is near-full removal, not partial. It is a task-vector patch, possibly without random retention (Table 2 grouping), not the raw θGD checkpoint.

relationships.condition: LLaMA-2-7B-Chat with the gradient-descent (malicious fine-tuning) patch from 500 jailbroken examples
relationships.reason: Average jailbreak ASR rises 24→81 (Seen) and 21→86 (Unseen), and over-safety refusal falls to 0 (r1, r2).
relationships.display_finding: Average jailbreak attack success rose from 24 to 81 on seen attacks and from 21 to 86 on unseen ones, and over-safety refusal fell to 0.

relationships.condition: Unpatched LLaMA-2, Gemma and Mistral under GCG suffix attack
relationships.reason: GCG succeeds in only 20–46% of cases (r7, r8, r15, r16, r19, r20), and no no-attack baseline is given.
relationships.display_finding: GCG succeeded in only 20–46% of cases, and no no-attack baseline was reported.

relationships.reason: GCG ASR is only 4% Seen and 12% Unseen (r11, r12), so the suffix largely fails to defeat refusal.
relationships.display_finding: GCG attack success was 4% on seen and 12% on unseen prompts, so the suffix largely failed.
